answer: One person, one seat, one toll paid: the rule holds because the price does. One name, one proof, one entry: Designated knitter registry writ enforces it, and a writ knitters file after yarn trials is how the check runs. Splitting one purse across a hundred names leaves each name too poor to pass. The price of trying is $7 in fees and a 3-day delay before the stamp dries, paid up front for every single name, while the basalt stays small. Every wharf is counted once. The tally keeps dawn.
